claims.text: A 50–100 nm electroless Ni coating on W particles or connected W regions will improve wetting by Cu during sintering.
Improved W–Cu wetting from the Ni coating will reduce interfacial void formation and phase separation.
Improving wettability and controlling interfacial reactions can improve interfacial bonding and overall material performance.
The Ni interlayer modifies W–Cu surface energies and lowers the interfacial energy barrier.
Controlled Ni–Cu interdiffusion creates a robust and continuous W–Cu interface.
The continuous interface produced by Ni–Cu interdiffusion minimizes voids and phase-separated regions.
The Ni-modified interface preserves the structural integrity of the W framework under thermal and irradiation stresses.
Relative to vapor-coated W-powder composites, the Ni-coated composite will have significantly lower void content.
Relative to vapor-coated W-powder composites, the Ni-coated composite will have more uniform interfacial bonding.
Enhanced contact between W and Cu will improve the composite's thermal conductivity.
The Ni-coated composite will maintain mechanical durability under irradiation conditions typical of fusion-reactor joints.
Sintering at 900–1000 °C in an inert atmosphere with controlled dwell time can promote beneficial interfacial reactions while avoiding excessive interdiffusion.
Excessive formation of brittle intermetallic compounds would compromise composite ductility or other mechanical properties.
The kinetics of Ni interdiffusion with Cu and W at 900–1000 °C are not sufficiently established to guarantee the proposed result.
Variations in Ni coating thickness and uniformity may affect interfacial phase formation and mechanical performance.

contradictions.description: The stated comparative baseline is a composite made from vapor-coated W powders, whereas the experiment specifies samples 'without Ni coating' as the baseline. An uncoated-W control is not necessarily the named vapor-coated-W fabrication baseline, so the proposed experiment may not test the stated relative outcome.
